rule: ปาก splits between the organ and the speaking, and sense 7 (พูด) takes the larger share — seventeen of twenty-seven. The test is the gloss, not the literal act: ปิดปาก, หุบปาก and เย็บปาก all describe closing a mouth but are glossed ไม่พูด / หยุดพูด, so they are about silence and file with speech. So do the characterisations of how a person talks (ปากหวาน, ปากจัด, ปากหมา, ปากโป้ง, ปากปลาร้า, ปากเสีย, ปากเปียก, ฝีปาก), the slips (หลุดปาก, พลั้งปาก), the register (ภาษาปาก) and the testimony (ปากคำ). Sense 1 keeps the mouth as a physical organ doing physical things — kissing, whistling, clicking, pursing, tasting — and it keeps ปากกา and ปากไก่, since sense 1 covers animals too and a nib is named for a bird's beak. Sense 3, the rim of an opening, takes only ปากเหว, the mouth of the chasm.
